name: Nationalpark Hohe Tauern
kurzbeschreibung: The largest national park in Austria, featuring glaciers, waterfalls, and a unique alpine world of wildlife and flora. Hohe Tauern Nationalpark in Tirol and Kärnten offers breathtaking landscapes and rare ecosystems.
beschreibung:
Overview

Covering an expansive 1,856 square kilometers, the Nationalpark Hohe Tauern represents Austria's oldest and largest nature reserve and the most extensive national park in the European Alps. Spanning the federal provinces of Tyrol (East Tyrol), Salzburg, and Carinthia, its Tyrolean realm encompasses some of the most breathtaking high-alpine ecosystems on Earth. Guarded by more than 260 summits exceeding 3,000 meters—crowned by Austria's highest peak, the Großglockner (3,798 m), and the glaciated Großvenediger (3,657 m)—the park preserves an untouched wilderness. Mighty glaciers, rushing meltwater torrents, over 500 crystal-clear alpine tarns, old-growth stone pine forests, and verdant alpine pastures shelter the famous Alpine "Big Five": the alpine ibex, chamois, bearded vulture, golden eagle, and alpine marmot. The administrative and interpretive hub of the East Tyrolean sector is situated in Matrei in Osttirol, where the state-of-the-art Nationalparkhaus greets travelers with multimedia exhibits.

Route & Requirements

Hiking possibilities inside Hohe Tauern span barrier-free educational pathways to rigorous high-alpine glacial traverses. A standout family classic is the Umbal Waterfalls Theme Trail in the Virgental valley (starting from Ströden parking area): cantilevered viewing platforms suspend visitors directly over the roaring glacial gorge of the Isel river (1.5 to 2 hours round trip, easy grade T1). Another crown jewel is Innergschlöss near Matrei, celebrated as "the most beautiful valley head in the Eastern Alps." From Matreier Tauernhaus, visitors stroll or take horse-drawn carriage shuttles past the historic rock chapel to access the Glacier Trail, showcasing the retreating tongue of the Schlatenkees glacier (4 to 5 hours, 550 m elevation gain, moderate grade T2). Serious ascents of the Großglockner or Großvenediger strictly necessitate crampons, rope teams, glacier expertise, and certified mountain guides. Rigid hiking boots, thermal layers, and high-SPF sun protection are mandatory park-wide. Dogs are welcome on leashes to protect sensitive wildlife.

Visit & Arrival

By rail, travelers arrive via ÖBB trains into Lienz station, boarding frequent regional VVT buses connecting directly to Matrei in Osttirol, Prägraten (Ströden trailhead), and Kals am Großglockner. Drivers travel the Felbertauern highway B108 (an all-weather toll route linking Salzburg province with East Tyrol) right into Matrei. Feeder roads lead to large pay parking lots at Matreier Tauernhaus, Ströden, and Lucknerhaus.

Tips

Book a guided excursion with a National Park Ranger: equipped with high-powered Swarovski spotting scopes, rangers bring visitors eye-to-eye with soaring bearded vultures and herds of ibex. Don't miss the interactive "Glaciers.Life" exhibition at the Nationalparkhaus in Matrei (free admission). At mountain chalets, sample traditional East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen and artisanal Pregler schnapps.
